Author: Pushpendra Singh Bhati Bench: Pushpendra Singh Bhati

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Misc(Pet.) No. 3271 / 2017 Lokesh Kumar S/o Shri Deva Ji, By Caste Rawal Brahmin, R/o Kothar, Tehsil Bali, Distt. Pali.
 ----Petitioner  Versus The State of Rajasthan  ----Respondent _____________________________________________________ For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Pradeep Shah For Respondent(s) :Mr. MS Panwar, PP _____________________________________________________  HON'BLE DR. entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Petitioner has preferred this misc. petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.292/2017 of Police Station Sumerpur, Distt. Pali, for the offences under Sections 420, 486, 487,
272, 273 of IPC and Section 3 (1) (Z, Z) (11) Food Safety and Standard Act 2006.
2.

At the outset, counsel for the petitioner submits that on the bare reading of the FIR, there is no allegation against the present petitioner as he is neither the owner of the adulterated mustard oil nor the shop in question nor the transport in question and therefore, prima facie no case has been made out against him on the bare reading of the FIR.
3. The facts of the case as noticed by this Court are that ASI P.S. Sumerpur on 27.02.2016 at 11.15 P.M. receiving information pertaining to some person storing adulterated mustard oil in the shop of New Rajendra Transport at Rajendra Market, Sumerpur.

On the basis of aforementioned information ASI of P.S. Sumerpur reached the shop and seized 16 Carton Oil (2 of 2)
[CRLMP-3271/2017] under Section 102 of Cr.P.C. and the sample was taken and sent for FSL and the FSL report was received on 11.07.2016, on the basis of FSL report, present FIR has been filed.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner wants to submit a representation alongwith all the relevant documents before the concerned investigating authority.

5. Learned Public Prosecutor assures this Court that if the petitioner submits a representation along with all the necessary documents before the concerned investigating authority within a period of ten days from today, then the same shall be considered and decided strictly in accordance with law,
before completing the investigation.

sentences.text:
6. In light of the aforesaid assurance given by learned Public Prosecutor, the present misc. petition is disposed of with a direction to the concerned investigating authority that in case the petitioner submits a representation along with all the necessary documents before it within a period of ten days from today, then the same shall be considered and decided before completing the investigation,
strictly in accordance with law and as per the assurance given by the learned Public Prosecutor.
However, if during the investigation, the concerned investigating authority needs to arrest the petitioner, then the petitioner shall be given 15 days notice before making such arrest.
The petitioner shall be at liberty to approach this Court again, in case need arises.

(DR. PUSHPENDRA SINGH BHATI)J. sudheer Lokesh Kumar vs State on 3 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2074272/
